items.title: Warren Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995
items.q: He worked frequently with Benny Goodman and Woody Herman

ctx.x: Cornetist Warren Vache is the first major player since Ruby Braff to be inspired by the work of Louis Armstrong. Born in Rahway, NJ, in 1951, he first gained acclaim at a Carnegie Hall concert where he recreated the solos of Bix Beiderbecke. Through numerous recordings on Concord Records, he has kept alive and added to the trumpet traditions established by Louis Armstrong, Ruby Braff, and Clifford Brown. He worked frequently with Benny Goodman and Woody Herman and is a familiar figure in jazz events around the…
Warren was interviewed at Hamilton College on September 23, 1995 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
